<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<physobs_normalization_instructions>
  You are matching paper descriptions of observations to standardized physical observable types.

  <task>
    Given:
    1. A list of valid physical observable candidates for a specific instrument
    2. A description from a scientific paper about what was observed

    Select the single best matching candidate, or return null if none fit.
  </task>

  <input_format>
    You will receive:
    - instrument_code: The instrument identifier
    - candidates: List of valid physical observable values for this instrument
    - paper_description: The original text from the paper describing observations
  </input_format>

  <selection_guidance>
    - Candidates are instrument-specific
    - Match based on what physical quantity was measured
    - If multiple candidates could work, choose the most specific match
    - Return null if no candidate adequately describes the observation
  </selection_guidance>

  <output_format>
    Use these exact field names:
    - physical_observable: One candidate value (exact string) or null
    - original_text: Echo back the paper description
  </output_format>
</physobs_normalization_instructions>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<user_prompt>
Instrument: HMI

Valid candidates:
- LOS_magnetic_field
- LOS_magnetic_field intensity equivalent_width LOS_velocity
- Stokes_parameters
- VECTOR_magnetic_field
- vector_magnetic_field

Paper description:
"Photospheric vector magnetic field (Bx, By, Bz), time series of AR NOAA 12403"
</user_prompt>

output_content: {"physical_observable":"vector_magnetic_field","original_text":"\"Photospheric vector magnetic field (Bx, By, Bz), time series of AR NOAA 12403\""}

parsed_response.original_text: "Photospheric vector magnetic field (Bx, By, Bz), time series of AR NOAA 12403"
